hypotheses.statement: Let $d\ge3$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ be a nonempty connected open set, and let $u\in C(\Omega)$ be infinity-harmonic. Then $u\in C^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$.
If $u$ is infinity-harmonic in $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$, then $$U(y,b)=u(y)+b$$ is infinity-harmonic in $\Omega\times\mathbb{R}$.

The function $w$ is locally Lipschitz. For a fixed center $z$, both $L_r^+(w;z)$ and $L_r^-(w;z)$ are nondecreasing in $r$. For each fixed allowable radius, they are continuous as functions of the center.

Let $w$ be infinity-harmonic in $D$ and let $z\in D$. Every locally uniform limit, along a sequence $r_i\downarrow0$, of $$V_i(Y)=\frac{w(z+r_iY)-w(z)}{r_i}$$ is a linear function on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Such limits exist after passage to subsequences.

Let $g_j$ be continuous on open subsets of Euclidean spaces. Suppose that $\sum_{j=1}^N g_j(z_j)-\Psi(z_1,\ldots,z_N)$ has a local maximum at an interior product point, where $\Psi$ is $C^2$ near that point. Set $A=D^2\Psi$. For the sequence supplied by Lemma 11 and the normalization [eq:anisotropic-rescaling], a subsequence of the $v_i$ converges locally uniformly to a nonaffine function $v\in C(\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R})$ satisfying [eq:limit-pde] and [eq:limit-fit] with one finite constant $C_0$.

For a subsolution $f$ as in Lemma 16, $\mathcal{S}_\ell^+f(z)$ is nondecreasing in $\ell$ and $$\label{eq:subsolution-slope-order} \limsup_{\ell\downarrow0}\mathcal{S}_\ell^-f(z) \le\lim_{\ell\downarrow0}\mathcal{S}_\ell^+f(z).$$ The right side may equal $-\infty$. For a supersolution, $\mathcal{S}_\ell^-f(z)$ is nondecreasing and $$\limsup_{\ell\downarrow0}\mathcal{S}_\ell^+f(z) \le\lim_{\ell\downarrow0}\mathcal{S}_\ell^-f(z).$$ Consequently, for a solution both slopes are nondecreasing and $$\label{eq:hamiltonian} \lim_{\ell\downarrow0}\mathcal{S}_\ell^+f(z) =\lim_{\ell\downarrow0}\mathcal{S}_\ell^-f(z) =:H_f(z)\in[-\infty,\infty).$$ The function $H_f$ is upper semicontinuous.

Let $v$ be a continuous viscosity subsolution of [eq:limit-pde] on $\mathbb{R}^m\times I$, and fix positive weights $\theta_i$ with $\sum_{i=1}^N\theta_i=1$. Define $$V((y_i)_{i=1}^N,t)=\sum_{i=1}^N\theta_i v(y_i,t).$$ If a $C^2$ function $\Phi$ touches $V$ from above at $(Y_0,t_0)$, where $Y=(y_i)_{i=1}^N$, then $$\label{eq:common-time-inequality} D^2\Phi(Y_0,t_0) \left[\left( \bigl(\theta_i^{-1}\nabla_{y_i}\Phi(Y_0,t_0)\bigr)_{i=1}^N, 1\right)\right]\ge0.$$

Let $f\in C(\mathbb{R}^m\times(0,\infty))$ be a viscosity subsolution of [eq:limit-pde] with subquadratic spatial growth on compact time intervals. Then $(x,t)\mapsto\mathcal{C}_t f(x,t)$ is a viscosity subsolution of [eq:limit-pde] on $\mathbb{R}^m\times(0,\infty)$. For every $c\in\mathbb{R}$, the same holds for $(x,t)\mapsto\mathcal{C}_t f(x,t)-ct$.

At the state and steps above define $$\begin{aligned}
  D&=f(z)+f^{2\epsilon}(z)-2f^\epsilon(z),\\
  e&=f^\epsilon(z^-)+\frac{\epsilon}{2}|Q_-|^2-f(z),\\
  \widetilde D&=2g_\epsilon(z)-v(z)-\mathcal{M}_{2\epsilon}v(z),\\
  \widetilde e&=v(z)+\frac{\epsilon}{2}|Q_+|^2-g_\epsilon(z^+).
\end{aligned}$$ Here $D$ and $\widetilde D$ are the midpoint gaps for forward convexity and backward concavity. The quantities $e$ and $\widetilde e$ are the gaps from using $z$ as a competitor from the opposite step. All four quantities are nonnegative, and the exact drift identity and the velocity estimate are $$\label{eq:dp-drift}
\begin{split}
  \frac{J_\epsilon(z^+)+J_\epsilon(z^-)}{2}-J_\epsilon(z)
  &=\frac{D+e+\widetilde D+\widetilde e}{4\epsilon}\\
  &\ge\frac{D+e}{4\epsilon}\\
  &\ge c\bigl(|Q_+-Q_0|^2+|Q_--Q_0|^2\bigr),
  \qquad c=\frac{1}{16(1+\log2)}.
\end{split}$$
